fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. The psalm says, “With Your hand You drove out the nations and planted our fathers there; You crushed the peoples and cast them out.” So God did the driving out AND the planting. I think that's a heavy verse, since it speaks of peoples being crushed. The singers are crediting God's hand for all of it.

That's a warm idea, friend, but it's not in this song. The psalm says God “…crushed the peoples and cast them out.” I think that's a heavy line to sit with. It's God's hand clearing the land for their fathers.

Let's look at the verse again, friend. The psalm says, “You have made us a reproach to our neighbors, a mockery and derision to those around us.” That's the neighbors looking down on them, not up at them. Respect isn't in that verse.

Yes, baker. The psalmist says, “…would not God have discovered, since He knows the secrets of the heart?” So if they'd forgotten God's name or spread out their hands to a foreign god, God would have found out. That's the claim the psalmist is making here.

That's the word, baker. The psalmist says, “For our soul has sunk to the dust; our bodies cling to the earth.” That's about as low as a person can get. I think this one is heavy, since it's the sound of people worn all the way down.
